chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:
A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Only the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to the Imam; he does with him whatever he desires.'
I said, 'So is that delegated to him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is like the crime (blood money/diyyah).'

key_terms.الْجِنَايَةِ: Crime/Tort (specifically referring to bodily injury or blood money contexts)

ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the Imam's authority in punishing those who wage war against Allah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Imam’s authority over the hadd of al-muharibun is not absolute discretion (tafwid) but is bound by structured legal principles akin to jinayah (blood money/criminal liability). This distinction underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the Imam’s judicial power operates within a defined framework of equity and precedent, rather than arbitrary decree. The hadith thus serves as a critical link between Quranic revelation and the practical application of Islamic penal law by the divinely appointed leader.
